institution: Dr. Ram Manohar Lohia Institute of Medical Sciences, Lucknow
citation: Department of Microbiology, Dr. Ram Manohar Lohia Institute of Medical Sciences, Lucknow. Microbiology Newsletter, Issue 10 (published February 2023): annual antibiograms, January to December 2022. Lucknow: Dr. RMLIMS; 2023.
reporting: Percent susceptible (colour-coded >90%, 70 to 90%, <70%) with the number of isolates, by specimen (blood, sterile body fluids including CSF, respiratory, pus and other samples, urine) and organism or organism group; each row is one location (OPD, IPD or ICU), shown only by the colour of its Number cell. Candida: percent susceptible by specimen for isolates tested on request, not split by location.
method: AST method and breakpoint edition not stated for the antibiograms. The report's colistin and vancomycin MIC tables are from VITEK 2 COMPACT (bioMerieux) and cite CLSI M100 31st edition (2022) for colistin categories.

verification.note: Antibacterial tables (PDF pages 8 to 14): cell text parsed from the PDF text layer with pdfplumber (ruled table cells; rotated drug headers rebuilt from character positions), and the location of each row taken from the background colour of its Number cell sampled on the page rendered at scale 3 (OPD pink, IPD blue, ICU yellow, as in each page legend). Every value, every n and every row location was then compared by eye with the rendered pages, with the parsed text overlaid on each table image (scale 3): no differences. The values are percentages: they agree with the printed colour code (for example 77 on an amber 70 to 90% cell where n is 259) and several exceed the row n. The row n values also agree with the legible bars of the organism charts on the same pages (for example respiratory IPD Klebsiella 61, Pseudomonas 53, Acinetobacter 47; urine ICU Enterococcus 34, E. coli 30, Pseudomonas 30), which confirms the colour-based location of those rows. Antifungal table (page 18): parsed from the text layer and compared with the page image the same way. Page numbers are PDF page numbers (the printed page number is one lower on the antibiogram pages).

notes: Dr. RMLIMS Lucknow Microbiology Newsletter, Issue 10 (February 2023), annual antibiograms for January to December 2022. Each specimen page has organism tables whose rows are OPD, IPD (recorded as wards) and ICU strata identified only by the colour of the Number cell; the report prints rows only for organisms or groups it could report. To reach 30 isolates the report groups organisms: "Lactose fermenters" (E. coli, Citrobacter, Klebsiella and Enterobacter spp.) rows are not recorded because no organism key fits a mixed Enterobacterales group (see excluded). "Other Staphylococcus spp." is defined by the report as coagulase-negative staphylococci and is recorded as CoNS. "Pseudomonas spp." rows are recorded under the P. aeruginosa key, as printed. Specimens: "Body fluids" are sterile body fluids including CSF (recorded as sterile body fluids); "Respiratory specimen" includes sputum, BAL, throat swab, nasal swab, bronchial aspirate and endotracheal aspirate; "Pus" includes pus, pus swab, catheter tip, CVP line, shunt, tissue, bone marrow, genital and ear samples, stool and urethral swab (recorded as pus). Codes follow the report's abbreviation list (AB amphotericin B, MYC micafungin, CAS caspofungin, VRC voriconazole); NX, not in that list, is the norfloxacin column the urine pages annotate. Cells printed "-", "**" or blank are left out. Many rows have fewer than 30 isolates (the report's own rule is 30). The live URL returns 404; the PDF was downloaded from the Internet Archive capture of the same URL (2024-03-30).
issues: Second reader 2026-09-26: all 434 cells (the seeded sample of 108 included), all 42 row n values and all 42 row locations re-read against the page images (PDF pages 8 to 14 and 18, rendered at scale 3 to 4); 0 errors, nothing corrected; every table was read in full.

Row locations: the fill colour of every Number cell, taken from the PDF vector fills, was compared with each page legend (OPD pink, IPD blue, ICU yellow): all 42 agree with the recorded setting. The respiratory IPD Klebsiella pneumoniae cell (n 61) is a paler blue-grey but is nearest the IPD colour, and the IPD chart on that page shows Klebsiella 61.
Caution confirmed as printed: pus IPD Staphylococcus aureus (n 119) linezolid 88, on an amber (70 to 90%) cell; the OPD row prints 93.
Antifungal FLU column (9 values) confirmed as left out for the reason in excluded: the p7 abbreviation list defines FLU as flucytosine and FLC as fluconazole.

excluded.what: Lactose fermenters rows: blood IPD (n=77) and ICU (n=113), p8; body fluids IPD (n=184), p9; pus OPD (n=92) and IPD (n=349), p11
excluded.why: organism group (E. coli, Citrobacter, Klebsiella and Enterobacter spp. per the report's abbreviations) with no organism key; recording it under one species would mislabel the figures

excluded.what: 'Lactose fermenters other than Klebsiella pneumoniae' row, respiratory IPD (n=39), p10
excluded.why: mixed Enterobacterales group with no organism key

excluded.what: Organism isolation bar charts (OPD, IPD and ICU boxes on pp8 to 13)
excluded.why: embedded low-resolution images (about 180 x 230 pixels per chart): the data labels of the smaller bars and the legend entries are not reliably legible, so no counts are recorded; the row n values come from the Number column of each table

excluded.what: Sample totals per location (Specimen, Sterile, Growth, Contamination, NSG, Gram stain, pp8 to 13)
excluded.why: numbers of samples, not isolates of an organism

excluded.what: Colistin MIC distribution of Gram-negative isolates, VITEK 2 (p17)
excluded.why: percent of isolates at each MIC, not percent susceptible (CLSI 2022 has no susceptible category for colistin)

excluded.what: Vancomycin MIC distribution of Staphylococcus spp., VITEK 2 (p16)
Infection-control surveillance (air cultures and swabs) of the Super Speciality Block, the Hospital Block, RPG Hospital and district hospitals (pp14 to 15)
excluded.why: environmental and colonisation surveillance, not clinical isolates

excluded.what: Antifungal table (p18), FLU column: blood Candida parapsilosis 83; blood Candida auris 33; blood Candida albicans 64; blood Candida tropicalis 100; respiratory sample Candida tropicalis 50; respiratory sample Candida albicans 100; urine Candida auris 50; urine Candida tropicalis 83; urine Candida albicans 80; "-" for C. glabrata
excluded.why: the drug is uncertain: the abbreviation list (p7) defines FLU as flucytosine and FLC as fluconazole, but this table has no FLC column, its footnote offers fluconazole as the surrogate for other triazoles (which needs a fluconazole result in the table), and FLU is blank for C. glabrata, the species for which this laboratory left fluconazole, not flucytosine, blank in 2018 and 2020; recording it under either drug could mislabel it

counts of all Candida isolates (for example blood C. albicans 35), while antifungal testing was done only on request (the table n, e.g. 11); recording them as counts would report false count-table mismatches. The charts show no C. auris although the table lists 6 blood and 6 urine C. auris isolates tested.
